[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state senator [[Laura Kelly]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state secretary of state [[Kris Kobach]] to win her first term in office. On July 26, 2017, Governor [[Sam Brownback]] was nominated by President [[Donald Trump]] to serve as [[United States Ambassador-at-Large for International Religious Freedom]]. He was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on January 24, 2018;{{cite news|last1=Sullivan|first1=Sean|last2=Zauzmer|first2=Julie|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/pence-forced-to-break-tie-over-nomination-of-brownback-for-religious-freedom-post/2018/01/24/8509a9d2-014b-11e8-8acf-ad2991367d9d_story.html|title=Pence forced to break tie over nomination of Brownback for religious freedom post|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=January 24, 2018}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.kwch.com/content/news/470954763.html|title=Gov. Sam Brownback's last day in office is Jan. 31|last=Heilman|first=Nick Viviani and Matt|access-date=January 27, 2018|language=en|archive-date=January 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128021138/http://www.kwch.com/content/news/470954763.html|url-status=dead}} he resigned the governorship on January 31 and was succeeded by Lieutenant Governor [[Jeff Colyer]].{{cite news|last1=Smith|first1=Mitch|last2=Fortin|first2=Jacey|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/26/us/politics/sam-brownback-kansas-ambassador-international-religious-freedom.html?rref=us|title=Gov. Sam Brownback of Kansas Will Be Nominated as Religious Ambassador|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=July 26, 2017|access-date=July 27, 2017}} Colyer was eligible to seek a full term and announced his candidacy prior to becoming Governor of Kansas. In the August 7 primary, Colyer ran against CPA and incumbent Insurance Commissioner [[Ken Selzer]], Topeka doctor and 2006 Republican Kansas gubernatorial nominee [[Jim Barnett (Kansas politician)|Jim Barnett]], and Kobach. On August 7, 2018, Kobach defeated Colyer in the Republican gubernatorial primary by an initial margin of 191 votes,{{cite web|url=https://ent.sos.ks.gov/|title=Unofficial Kansas Election Results|website=ent.sos.ks.gov|access-date=August 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814222950/https://ent.sos.ks.gov/|archive-date=August 14, 2018|url-status=dead}} a lead that increased to 361 votes by August 14, although discrepancies in some counties needed resolution and provisional and absentee ballots may not have been counted in some counties.{{Cite news|url=https://www.kansascity.com/news/politics-government/election/article216631160.html|title=Kris Kobach continues to build his lead after Johnson County ballots tallied|last1=Woodall|first1=Hunter|last2=Vockrodt|first2=Steve|last3=Lowry|first3=Bryan|work=Kansas City Star|access-date=August 14, 2018|language=en-US}}[https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/powerpost/wp/2018/08/09/kobach-lead-over-colyer-cut-in-half-after-vote-tallying-error-discovered-in-kansas-gop-primary/ Kris Kobach, Trump ally and Kan. secretary of state, recuses himself from vote counting in his own GOP primary vs. Gov. Jeff Colyer], ''[[The Washington Post]]'', Amy B. Wang and Felicia Sonmez, August 9, 2018. Retrieved August 10, 2018.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wibw.com/content/news/Kobach-lead-falls-to-under-100-after-misreported-votes-discovered-490480031.html|title=More discrepancies found in Kobach-Colyer vote totals|first=Melissa Brunner; Nick|last=Viviani|website=www.wibw.com}} Colyer conceded the Republican nomination after the final votes were tallied, in which Kobach's margin grew slightly.{{cite news |last=Feuerborn |first=Mark |publisher=KSNT.com |title=Colyer concedes to Kobach a week after Kansas GOP primary |date=August 14, 2018 |access-date=August 14, 2018 |url=https://www.ksnt.com/news/local-news/colyer-concedes-to-kobach-a-week-after-kansas-gop-primary/1369315216}} Kelly easily won the Democratic nomination[https://www.vox.com/2018/8/7/17660516/live-results-kansas-primary-elections-2018-kobach-colyer Live results for the Kansas primary elections Kris Kobach is challenging incumbent Jeff Colyer in the GOP primary for governor.], ''[[Vox (website)]]'', Ella Nilsen and Li Zhou, August 7, 2018. Retrieved August 10, 2018. and won the general election, assuming office on January 14, 2019. Businessman Greg Orman, who finished second as an independent in the [[United States Senate election in Kansas, 2014|2014 U.S. Senate race]] against incumbent Republican [[Pat Roberts]], ran for governor as an independent candidate.{{cite news|last=Rucker|first=Philip |date=November 4, 2014 |title=Battle for the Senate: How the GOP did it |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/battle-for-the-senate-how-the-gop-did-it/2014/11/04/a8df6f7a-62c7-11e4-bb14-4cfea1e742d5_story.html |access-date=August 9, 2018 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} As, aside from a two-term limit for incumbents, the [[Constitution of Kansas]] places no limitations of any kind on who may seek the office, several teenagers (including one who had never been to the state), filed to run for governor, drawing media attention.{{cite web |url=http://www.kansascity.com/news/politics-government/article175956836.html |title=As third teen joins Kansas governor race, consider this: No rule says a dog can't run |last=Woodall |first=Hunter |date=September 28, 2017 |website=The Kansas City Star |access-date=September 29, 2017}} A debate took place on September 5 between the three candidates that consistently polled above 5%.{{Cite web|url=https://www.jocobar.org/page/Govdebate2018|title=Gov Debate 2018 - Johnson County Bar Association|website=www.jocobar.org}} Polls in late August had Kelly and Kobach running close with Orman polling in the single digits.{{Cite web|url=http://underthedomeks.org/new-poll-shows-dead-heat-in-race-for-kansas-governor/|title=New Poll Shows "Dead Heat" in Race for Kansas Governor | Under The Dome KS}} Kelly's win continued a streak of party turnover for governor of Kansas, as Kansas has not elected two consecutive governors of the same party since [[William H. Avery (politician)|William Avery]] succeeded fellow Republican [[John Anderson Jr.]] following the [[1964 Kansas gubernatorial election|1964 election]], and neither major party has held the governorship for longer than eight consecutive years since Republican [[John McCuish]] left office in 1957.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/without-a-clear-primary-winner-the-kansas-gop-might-be-at-a-disadvantage/2018/08/10/0866d2ee-9cb2-11e8-843b-36e177f3081c_story.html?noredirect=on Without a clear primary winner, the Kansas GOP might be at a disadvantage].
